red_flags: ROI of 7.9% is well below the 20% threshold for fix-and-flip deals
Purchase price at 65.3% of ARV — while below the 85% threshold, the renovation costs are eating all margin
Holding period of 7 months with $2,607/month carrying costs = $18,249 in holding alone
Phoenix market has seen 12.3% price appreciation over last year — buying at peak may compress margins if market corrects
Renovation budget of $38.69/sqft appears low for a full gut-reno in 2026 Phoenix labor market
Interest rate of 9.25% is high — hard money rates have been elevated; this deal assumes favorable terms
green_flags: Purchase price represents only 65.3% of ARV — significant spread on paper
Neighborhood has seen $140K+ appreciation over last 3 years
Property sits on larger lot (6,500 sqft) vs neighborhood median of 5,200 sqft
No environmental or zoning issues identified

market_context.note: Phoenix market remains strong but prices have surged. Competition from cash buyers is intense in the $300-400K range.

due_diligence_checklist: Verify ARV with 3 licensed appraisers (not just comps)
Get contractor bids — not estimates — for all renovation line items
Inspect foundation and slab (Phoenix soil expansion risk)
Check for permits on any unpermitted work by previous owner
Title search for HOA liens or special assessments
Verify financing terms — 9.25% hard money may not be available at that rate in current market
action_items: Walk away unless purchase price can be negotiated below $210K (requires ~$35K additional discount)
If pursuing, renegotiate renovation contract with fixed-price bids
Consider holding as rental instead — 5.2% yield is marginal but eliminates flip risk
analyst_note: This deal fails the fundamental test: after all costs, the profit margin is only 7.9%. In Phoenix's competitive market, any delay in selling or unexpected renovation issue pushes this into negative territory. The spread looks attractive on paper (65% of ARV), but renovation costs and carrying charges consume most of it. This is a classic case where the deal looks good until you add real-world friction.
